structured_stats.description:
The '''Scout''' is one of two starter towers obtained upon joining the game for the first time, with the other being the [[Sniper]].

The '''Scout''' is very cheap in comparison to other towers, meaning it can be placed right from the start of the game. However, the '''Scout''' has low DPS, even at higher levels, meaning it is not effective later on during the game. In [[PVP]] mode, it has far higher DPS than in regular modes, though it is still lower than most other options.

The '''Scout''' is considered an early-game tower due to its low cost and low overall damage.

==Description==
The '''Golden Scout''' is a upgraded version of the [[Scout]], obtained in the [[Golden Crate]] for {{Coins|50,000}}. It can also appear in the Daily Skin Store for {{Coins|55,000}}. You automatically unlock the '''Golden Scout's''' normal counterpart, the [[Scout]], when you first join in the game.

The '''Golden Scout''' is very cheap in comparison to other towers, meaning that it can be placed right from the start of the game. However, the '''Golden Scout''' has mediocre DPS, meaning that in harder modes it is not that effective later on during the game.

In comparison to its normal counterpart, the [[Scout]], it is considerably more expensive to upgrade. Despite this, the '''Golden Scout''' is significantly better than its normal counterpart because it has much higher DPS and efficiency. The '''Golden Scout''' is considered an early-game to mid-game tower, although it can handle the late-game with some support.

{{BossList|Default|Ref = Only the first '''Null Scout''' spawned in [[Outpost 16]] as a boss.}} }} ==Description== The '''Null Scout''', internally referred to as '''Corrupted Scout''', was an enemy that appeared in [[Outpost 16]], [[Banlands]] and [[Blind Faith]] as part of the [[Null & Void Event]]. It had higher health than every enemy that appeared before it while also being faster than every enemy except the [[Null Runner]]. It can be spawned by the [[Null Commander]], which boosts its [[Defense]] to 50%. ==Logbook Description== "''Scout stared down the Null Scout, and the creature stared back. Scout lifted one arm, and so it mirrored. He lifted the other — Null Scout followed. Scout quickly dropped both arms and aimed his weapons at the creature, who copied it. Then from the side, Trapper threw a landmine behind the Null Scout. Scout grinned, and stepped back — ... and Null Scout followed.''" ==Appearance== The '''Null Scout''' is a corrupted recreation of the [[Scout]]. It has light pink skin, torn black shirt and pants, and a single knee-pad. It has a few bandages wrapped around its hands. On its head, it wears a black cap and headphones, alongside cracked shades. Its entire body is covered in what appeared to be purple goo. ==Event Strategy== As this enemy only appears through [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. It is a very troublesome foe due to its high health and speed for when it appears. ==Appearance== The '''Scout''' is a robot that resembles the Level 0 and Level 3 Default [[Scout]]. It has pale skin, grey torso, sleeves and cap, dark grey backpack, dark green pants and knee-pad, and black shoe. The '''Scout's''' face is torn off and is hanging from its head, with multiple other parts of its body also being torn off, most notably its left shoulder, part of its left arm and its right foot, all of them also reveal the '''Scout's''' endoskeleton and wires. On death, it will shake and flail its arms around, emit yellow sparks, and then power down, with the yellow lights on its backpack turning off. It also plays a powering down sound when it dies. ==Strategy== *Cheap towers with high DPS, such as the [[Minigunner]], [[Crook Boss]], [[Brawler]] or multiple low Level [[Golden Scout]]s are recommended, as the '''Scout''' has quite high health. **More expensive towers like the [[Accelerator]] or [[Golden Minigunner]] can also be used, if you are able to afford them. *Towers that can slow down the '''Scout''', such as the [[Sledger]], [[Electroshocker]], [[Warden]] or [[Toxic Gunner]] can be quite helpful, as the '''Scout''' is fairly fast. **Do note that this is not possible when it first spawns, due to it being a [[Boss]] enemy. ==Description==
The '''Scout Plush''' is an official Paradoxum Games toy. It was made by Juniper Creates™. The plushie offers the Default Level 4 [[Scout]] skin. Anybody who bought the toy from the Merch Shop would get the [[Scout/Gallery#Plushie|{{Color|Other|Plushie}}]] skin for the [[Scout]]. If bought on the [https://shop.paradoxum.games/ Paradoxum Games store], it will not come with any rewards.

It is made out of plush fabric and Polypropylene cotton, it is 11.81 inches tall, 8.26 inches wide and 8.66 inches deep, or 29.99 centimetres tall, 20.98 centimetres wide and 21.99 centimetres deep. 

A tree is planted for every order of the '''Scout Plush'''.

==Official Description==
*'''Online'''
*:Scout reporting for duty! Your new gaming companion has arrived.

==Prices & Stores==
Prices vary by country due to shipping costs and local currency. The '''Scout Plush''' can be purchased on the official [https://shop.paradoxum.games/ Paradoxum Games online store] for for $34.99. It is currently unavailable.

Before April 2025, it could be purchased for $29.99. During the Black Friday 2024 Sale, it could be bought for $22.49.

==Description==
The '''Damage Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's damage, making them stronger. It is displayed on the tower itself with the icon of an arm with muscle.

==Mechanics==
'''Damage Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Damage × (1 + Damage Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Damage Buff''' is the debuff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The damage increased by the '''Damage Buff''' will always round down to the nearest integer. For example, a tower that deals 5 damage with a 50% '''Damage Buff''' will deal 7 damage, instead of 7.5.

Multiple towers are not fully affected by the buff. A full list of towers affected fully, partially or that are unaffected can be found below.
{{DamageBuff}}

==Applied By==
The following towers or consumables can apply the '''Damage Buff''' to other towers or itself:
*[[DJ Booth]] (Passive)
*[[Mercenary Base]] (Passive)
*[[Damage Flag]] (Passive)
*[[War Machine]] (Passive)
*[[Medic]] (''Ubercharge'' ability)
*[[Warden]] (When parrying)

The following event features can apply the '''Damage Buff''' to towers:

* [[Justice]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])
* [[The Chariot]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])

The following towers used to have the '''Damage Buff''':
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Crook Boss]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Minigunner]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Pyromancer]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Scout]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Cowboy]] (Passive)
*[[Militant|John]] (''Enraging Shout'' ability)
*[[Slasher|Shredder]] (''Knife Throw'' ability)
*[[Cowboy]] (''Wildest of the West and Gold Rush'' abilities'')''
*[[Gladiator]] (''Sharp Edge'' ability'')''

The following tower used to apply the '''Damage Buff''' to other towers:
*[[Militant|John]] (''Enraging Shout'' ability)

The following removed towers had the '''Damage Buff''':
*{{Color|Platinum}} [[Crook Boss]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Platinum}} [[Minigunner]] (Passive)

related_pages.title: Firerate Bug
related_pages.wikitext_excerpt:
{{Removed|date = 6th of June 2026}}
{{Improve|this page and majority of tower/unit pages require updating}}
The '''Firerate Bug''', also known as the '''RoF (Rate of Fire) Bug''', was a bug that slightly increased the firerate of all towers and units. This increase was not displayed on the statistics in the game. This bug significantly affected the statistics of fast-firing towers, such as the [[Minigunner]] and [[Ace Pilot]], by significantly decreasing their DPS, whereas slow-firing towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Sniper]] were hardly affected.

This has been fixed as of the 6th of June 2026, and all firerate statistics in the game are considered to be accurate unless affected by a different unrelated bug.

{{RightTOC}}

==Prior to 5th of June 2026==
The '''Firerate Bug''' affects all towers and units that can directly attack enemies, meaning the only towers that are not affected are the [[Farm]], [[Medic]] and the [[Firework Technician]] and the only units that are not affected are the [[Humvee]], [[Humvee 2]], [[Elf]], [[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]], [[Skeleton (Unit)|Skeleton]], [[Giant Skeleton (Unit)|Giant Skeleton]] and [[Hallow Guard (Unit)|Hallow Guard]]. The '''Firerate Bug''' does not affect the firerate of some secondary attacks towers or units may perform, some damage-over-time effects applied by towers (like burn from the [[Pyromancer]]) or certain other cooldowns.

The '''Firerate Bug''' increases the firerate of a tower/unit depending on its firerate, which can vary anywhere between 0.017 and 0.032 seconds. The firerate increase affects fast firing towers the most; for example, the [[Minigunner]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 0.09, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 0.117, decreasing its DPS from 166.67 to 128.20, which is a decrease of 38.47 DPS, or a loss of about 23.08 DPS. Meanwhile, slow firing towers are barely affected by it; for example, the [[Ranger]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 8, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 8.025, decreasing its DPS from 156.26 to 155.76, which is a decrease of 0.30 DPS, or a loss of 0.2% DPS.

The [[Firerate Buff]] is also affected by the '''Firerate Bug''', making it less effective. For example, the Level 4 [[Minigunner]] without the '''Firerate Bug''' with a 50% firerate boost should have a firerate of 0.06, but with the '''Firerate Bug''' it has a firerate of 0.083. This means that its DPS with a 50% firerate boost is decreased from 250 to 180.72, which is a decrease of 69.28 DPS, or a loss of 27.71% DPS.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units is increased by specific values based on the firerate. While technically possible to calculate by hand, due to the effort it would take, it is overall recommended to either use [[Help:Neowtext#ROFBUG|Neowtext]] or [https://fiheron.github.io/dps-calc/ an online calculator].

==Prior to the 9th of January 2023==
Prior to the 9th of January 2023, the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was higher than it currently is. The firerate increase was generally around 0.03 seconds. For towers, the firerate increase remained at around 0.008 seconds.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units after the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]] and before the 9th of January 2023 is increased by 0.008 and 0.03 respectively, unless stated otherwise. This does not, however, mean the actual value is this; it can vary between towers and even between matches.

==Prior to the Violent Night Update==
Prior to the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]], the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was lower than it was before the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]]. The firerate increases could be anywhere between 0.008 and 0.017 seconds, but the increase was generally around 0.008 seconds. This is the same as the current situation.

Build up chill to slow and freeze enemies in their tracks!|Store Description}} |-|Version 3 = {{QuoteBox|Chill enemies to a slow freeze!|Store Description}} |-|Version 2 = {{QuoteBox|Shoot an ice beam, freezing targets for a few seconds.|Store Description}} |-|Version 1 = {{QuoteBox|Freeze zombies temporarily with a freeze ray!|Former Store Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Freezer''' is a ground [[Towers|tower]] that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for {{Coins|650}}. The '''Freezer''' targets a single enemy and fires a ''Frost Ray'', chilling the enemy and slowing it down. The chillness slowness effect stacks with each hit multiple times. This chillness effect also deals damage over time, chipping away the health of enemies affected by it. Starting from Level 2, it can freeze enemies. When the chillness slowness effect is higher than the max slowdown, the enemy will be frozen, which generally when targeting a single enemy takes four or five shots. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with [[Freeze Immunity]] also cannot be frozen, slowed down or have their defense dropped by the '''Freezer'''. At Level 3+, the '''Freezer''' fires in bursts, with a short delay between them. Additionally, at Level 3+, it drops defense by 10% every tick. It can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%. On top of this, it will also start dealing damage over time with its chill at Level 3. Additionally at Level 4, the '''Freezer''' gains the ability to throw a '''Frost Grenade''', freezing enemies within an explosion radius. The '''Freezer''' does well as an all-rounder support tower. Due to its generally low price and decent DPS, the '''Freezer''' can be a solid choice for early-game defense to mid game with very good cost efficiency. Towards late game, the '''Freezer''' is useful for stalling, defense melting and deal additional DPS through its damage over time, though its DPS is insufficient to deal with late-game waves alone. The '''Freezer''' has [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] detection from Level 0 and [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] detection from level 2.
